authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Verifies visible CORE teaching, practice and assessment for why an operating system is required and its memory, file, security, hardware and process management roles.
Verifies every named utility category, including formatter and disk contents analysis/repair, without allowing encryption to replace a required category.
Adds explicit teaching that software under development commonly reuses existing program-library code, with developer benefits and DLL dependency/version boundaries.
Directly distinguishes the need for an assembler, compiler and interpreter from their input languages and translation behaviour.
Teaches and assesses separate compiler and interpreter benefits and drawbacks, with scenario-based justification and two assessment forms.
Teaches and assesses Java console mode as partly compiled from source to bytecode and partly interpreted or JIT-compiled by the JVM, rejecting universal machine-code claims.
Covers context-sensitive prompts, dynamic syntax checks, prettyprint, expand/collapse, single stepping, breakpoints, variable/expression inspection and a report window with direct assessment.
Replaces the assembler infographic so target machine code, object modules, conditional linking and executable output are no longer presented as interchangeable.
Replaces the translator comparison infographic with separate compiler, interpreter and assembler paths and an explicit linker-if-required boundary.
